references.text: The glory of the Lord was revealed in the pillar of cloud that led the people of Israel through the wilderness, demonstrating God's visible presence among His people.
The glory of the Lord appeared on Mount Sinai in a cloud, and the Israelites saw it as a consuming fire.
The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle in the form of a cloud, confirming God's presence among the people.
The glory of the Lord appeared in the cloud at the tent of meeting when the people grumbled, just as in the wilderness.
The glory of the Lord was revealed to the entire congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
At the dedication of Solomon's temple, a cloud filled the house of the Lord, and the priests could not serve because of the glory of the Lord.
Ezekiel describes the glory of the Lord surrounded by a radiant brilliance, like the rainbow in the cloud.
The glory of the Lord lifted itself up from the cherubim, and the house was filled with the cloud.
At Jesus' transfiguration on the mountain, a bright cloud came over the disciples, and God's voice spoke from the cloud.
Jesus was taken up in a cloud at His ascension, linking to God's glory that is revealed in the cloud.
Parallel account of the glory of the Lord being revealed in the cloud when the congregation turns toward the sanctuary.
Thematic parallel where the glory of the Lord is revealed to the people after leaders have performed holy acts.
Parallel account of the glory of the Lord being revealed at the entrance of the tent of meeting during a crisis.
Typological parallel where the visible revelation of the glory of the Lord leads to public worship both in the wilderness and at the temple dedication.
